High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Deptt. Of Home

Lucknow Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant Umesh Yadav with a prayer to enlarge her on bail in Case Crime No.249 of 2021, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. Police Station Baghrai, District Pratapgarh.

Learned counsel for the applicant has invited attention of this Court towards the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in which she has levelled allegation that three persons including the applicant had abducted the prosecutrix when she had gone to ease herself.
They had taken her to Fatehpur and committed rape against her on the threat of gun point.
Thereafter the applicant had brought her to Lucknow and there she was kept in room for five days and rape was committed.
Learned counsel contended that the prosecutrix is aged about 30 years and married lady and it appears that it is a case of consent because she did not raised any alarm to make protest.
It is unbelievable that for five days, she remained at Lucknow and rape was committed and no alarm was raised by her.
Learned counsel further submitted that medical report is not supporting the prosecution case.

Learned counsel further contended that in the statement of local residents, it was found that other co-accused were falsely implicated due to enmity and they have been exonerated and charge sheet has been filed against the applicant only.
The applicant has no criminal history.

sentences.text: 1 The applicant is in jail since 11.09.2021.
Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and contended that the applicant is involved in committing the heinous crime, therefore, the applicant does not deserve any mercy.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits, after hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the nature of statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 Cr.P.C. medical report which does not support the prosecution case, therefore, I find it to be a fit case for bail.

Let the applicant, Umesh Yadav be released on bail in the above case crime number on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
